challenges.name: idempotency-checks
challenges.title: Write the idempotency checks for POST /orders
challenges.description: Couriers' phones retry `POST /orders` after a timeout, and last month some customers were charged twice. The API team says idempotency keys are implemented; the only test sent each request once. The editor holds `tests/test_idempotency.py` with the five checks missing, each marked by a `# [ ]` line; some pieces test the wrong thing on purpose. Fill every line so that the suite proves the contract in the docstring: a replay returns the first answer marked `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, a reused key with another body gets 422, a duplicate during processing gets 409, a retry after a lost response never creates a second order, and a request without a key gets 400. Run plays your checks against a correct API and against APIs with one known defect each: every defect must be caught by the right checks, and the correct API must pass them all.
hints: A check is only as good as the defect it catches. For each check, name the broken API that would pass it, then add the assertion that makes it fail.

Compare more than the status: the replay's body (same order id) and its header, the number of orders the customer has after a retry, and the status of the request that arrives while the first one is still running.

A check for a refund endpoint: `first = api.post("/refunds", json=R, headers={"Idempotency-Key": "r1"})`, `again = api.post(...same...)`, then `assert again.json() == first.json()` and `assert len(api.get("/refunds?order_id=5").json()) == 1`.

tests.name: The API that follows the contract passes every check
An API that ignores the key fails every check that sends one key twice
Replays without the Idempotent-Replayed header, and a reused key that is not refused
A duplicate processed during the first request, and a key stored only after responding
Requests without a key accepted, next to the correct API
